reason: The cited evidence shows that short-range ordering can enhance strength and ductility in CoFeNi (E1) and that chemical heterogeneities influence deformation mechanisms in CoCrFeNi (E2), but none of the passages involve the Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni system, compare quinary to quaternary/ternary subsets, or demonstrate that adding a constituent increases lattice distortions and ordering during deformation. E3 and E4 are largely irrelevant to the specific mechanistic claims.
premises: Additional constituent in quinary alloy enhances chemical complexity, inducing larger and more heterogeneous local lattice distortions during deformation.
These distortions promote formation/evolution of nanoscale short-range chemical ordering.
Short-range ordering modifies dislocation mobility and activates nonconventional slip mechanisms.
This results in increased strain hardening and altered plasticity relative to quaternary/ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will show distinct evolution of local chemical ordering during deformation correlating with higher work-hardening capacity.
